questions.question: What is the key memory characteristic of a union?
options: A. Each member always has separate storage
B. Members share the same storage area
C. A union cannot contain numeric types
D. A union always uses one byte

questions.question: Why should a union member generally be interpreted according to the member through which the value was most recently stored?
options: A. Because all members hold independent values
B. Because members share the same storage
C. Because only the first member exists
D. Because unions cannot contain integers

questions.question: What is the purpose of enum in C?
options: A. To define a set of named integer constants

questions.question: If enum Color { RED, GREEN, BLUE }; is declared, what value is assigned to RED by default?
In enum Color { RED, GREEN, BLUE };, what is the default value of BLUE?
Can an enum constant be explicitly assigned a value?
options: D. Only when the value is zero

questions.question: Which generally requires enough storage for all its members, subject to padding and implementation details?
Which generally has storage sufficient for its largest member, subject to alignment and implementation details?
Why might a union be useful in embedded systems?
options: A. It can allow different interpretations of the same storage when used correctly
B. It automatically prevents all memory corruption
C. It always increases memory usage
